properties.name: weakcrypto:config
properties.value: skill pq-crypto, 1 worker, max iterations 400, build bbcd802706e4

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: SHA-1 across the tree: the OpenCL kernel library, hashcat dynamic-mode recipes (src/dynamicx.c maps modes 110/4400/4700...), the Rust dynamic-hash DSL test recipes, and hundreds of module sites (Kerberos, WPA KCK, GPG CAST5 key derivation via SHA1(salt||password), SHA-1-based formats). SHA-1 is collision-broken classically and Grover-weakened; it is both an attack target and, in places like the GPG mode's KDF, the format's actual protection.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: MD5 across the tree: the OpenCL kernel library, dynamic-mode recipes (md5($p), md5($p.$s), chained md5(sha1($p))...), the Rust dynamic-hash DSL, and hundreds of hashcat cracking modes plus their test generators. MD5 is collision-broken; here it is overwhelmingly the attacked format.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: RC4 in hashcat: the OpenCL kernel cipher library (inc_cipher_rc4.h — SET_KEY8/32, rc4_init_40/72/104 for the WEP/WPA key-length variants) and modules/test modules for RC4-based formats (WEP 10400/10401/10402/10403, Kerberos RC4-HMAC, MS Office legacy, PDF RC4). RC4 is a broken stream cipher; here it is the attacked format.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: ECB modes across hashcat: AES-128/192/256-ECB NOKDF modules 26401-26403 (PT = $salt, key = $pass), the ECB primitive inside the XTS construction (lib/xts.py), and the LM hash (mode 3000: DES-ECB encrypting KGS!@#$% with the password-derived key). Deterministic ECB is what makes these formats crackable; it is format-inherent, not a choice made by this codebase.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: 3DES across hashcat: raw 3DES modes (14100 PT=$salt,key=$pass), PKCS#8 private-key containers (module_24410: PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA1 + 3DES/AES-CBC with PKCS_CIPHER_3DES selection and IV-length checks), MS Office/legacy formats, and their test generators. 3DES's 112-bit security and 64-bit block make it weak today — the tool cracks it.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: DES usage across hashcat test modules: the LM hash (m03000, DES-ECB over KGS!@#$%), Oracle DES-CBC (m03100), NetNTLM challenge-response DES-ECB (m05500), Lotus Notes DES-ECB (m08500/08501). DES is brute-forceable on commodity hardware — that is precisely why these formats are crackable; the tool implements and attacks it.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Weak/legacy password-hash sites (15 of 29 paged, uniform): the vendored yescrypt's PBKDF2_SHA256 self-tests at 1/2/4096/16M iterations with 16-32 byte outputs (yescrypt is built on PBKDF2-SHA256) and the generic Python hash-bridge plugin (Python/generic_hash.py hashlib.sha256 salted password-hash oracle for custom modes). These are the password-storage algorithms hashcat attacks; low iteration counts belong to the self-tests and legacy formats, not to a protection decision made by this codebase.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: MD4 across hashcat's test modules (all 19 pending sites seen): NTLM nthash (m05500/m05600/m12800/15310/15910/31500/31600/36500), MS DCC (m15300/15900/31600), salted MD4 chains (m01100/m31500), md5(md4($p)) hybrids (m31300), Kerberos RC4 keys (lib/kerberos_rc4.py). MD4 is fully broken; it remains the KDF inside NTLM — the world's most-cracked hash. The Rust dynamic_hash bridge also ships the md4 crate (Cargo.toml md4 = "0.10.2") for md4() recipe evaluation. Attacked-format inventory.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: HMAC-MD5 generation in hashcat test tools: Kerberos RC4-HMAC (lib/kerberos_rc4.py), NetNTLMv2 (lib/netntlmv2.py), raw HMAC-MD5 modes 50/60, and the WPA MIC (m02500/m02501). The repo computes genuine HMAC-MD5 digests as crack targets; HMAC-MD5 is a cryptographically broken MAC.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Blowfish in hashcat test-vector generators: ECB (m09000), CFB with PBKDF2-derived keys (m18600), CBC (m36400). Genuine Blowfish usage — the attacked formats (legacy app containers) use Blowfish; Blowfish's 64-bit block makes it birthday-bound.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Unauthenticated AES-CBC as required by attacked formats: LUKS v1 cbc-plain/plain64/essiv:sha256 (module_14600 selects HC_LUKS_CIPHER_MODE_CBC_* from the volume header), PKCS#12 keystores, and matching test generators. CBC without a MAC is format-inherent for disk encryption and keystore payloads hashcat attacks.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Low-iteration PBKDF2 instances: scrypt-jane calls scrypt_pbkdf2 with N=1 as its internal PRF (structural to scrypt-jane's ROMix/BlockMix design, not a weak config), yescrypt's self-test prints PBKDF2_SHA256 at 1/2/4096/16M iterations, and legacy-format test vectors whose low iteration counts are exactly why those formats are crackable (CWE-916 exposure lives in the attacked formats, not in this codebase's choices).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: bcrypt in hashcat's Rust dynamic_hash bridge: Cargo.toml pins bcrypt 0.17.1; eval.rs implements the bcrypt DSL (bcrypt/bcrypt2a/2b/2y versions, salt decode, hash_with_salt(data, cost, bin_salt)) — the bridge evaluates bcrypt recipes for dynamic modes; production costs are recipe-dictated (cost=4 appears only in unit tests). bcrypt is Grover-weakened, not Shor-broken.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: HMAC-SHA-1 across hashcat: NetIQ SSPR PBKDF2WithHmacSHA1 (module 32050), the legacy NSS/Firefox key4.db key-derivation chain (mozilla2hashcat.py k1/tk/k2 = hmac.new(chp, ..., hashlib.sha1)) used to decrypt Firefox stored passwords, raw HMAC-SHA1 mode 150, and WPA KCK/MIC paths. HMAC-SHA-1 is weak as a design choice but unbroken as a MAC; here it is the attacked/converted legacy format.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: hashcat's OpenCL secp256k1 library (inc_ecc_secp256k1.h): EC point arithmetic — precomputed table, public-key parse/transform — used by the Bitcoin/Electrum/Litecoin private-key cracking modules. Shor-vulnerable ECDLP over secp256k1; present to attack, not to protect. Changeable here (repo ships the kernel library).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Camellia and Kuznyechik implementations in hashcat's OpenCL cipher library (inc_cipher_camellia.h: FL/Feistel functions, camellia128/192/256 key schedule + encrypt/decrypt; inc_cipher_kuznyechik.h): shipped kernel algorithms used by disk-encryption and GOST-family cracking modes. Regional/national ciphers present in the tool's attack surface.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Static IV/nonce handling in hashcat's format converters and test-vector generators: mozilla2hashcat.py reproduces Firefox key4.db's stored IV for AES-CBC decryption (the attacked format's IV, prefixed 040e), pyserpent.py uses a zero IV for Serpent test vectors, m13200 uses the AES key-wrap constant a6a6a6a6..., others carry format-mandated constants. These IVs are part of the formats being cracked/converted, not protection choices made by this codebase.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: SHA-224 digest generation across hashcat test modules (modes 1300, 1310, 1320, 26700 SNMPv3, 34400 sha224(sha224($p))) — hashlib.sha224 builds crackable vectors; SHA-224 has the weakest margin of the SHA-2 family in the tree.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: bcrypt at work factor 4 in unit tests of hashcat's Rust dynamic_hash bridge (tests.rs recipe strings like bcrypt(cost=4,...)) — low cost chosen to keep unit tests fast; the same DSL supports production costs. Real bcrypt invocations through the Rust bcrypt crate.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: AES-CMAC via PyCryptodome (CMAC.new(ptk/kck, ciphermod=AES)) computing WPA/WPA2/WPA3 MICs in test-vector generators for modes 2500/2501/22000/22001. Genuine CMAC use; the tool attacks these handshakes.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: CFB/OFB/CTR mode usage in hashcat test tools: AES-CFB for GPG symmetric payloads (lib/gpg.py), CAST-128-CFB for GPG mode 17040, Blowfish-CFB (m18600), AES-OFB (m34700). Genuine stream-mode encryptions matching the attacked formats; the modes provide no integrity (format-inherent).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: SM3 (Chinese national hash standard) — hashcat mode 31100: dynamic-mode recipe entry in src/dynamicx.c and module_31100.c HASH_RECIPE. The tool cracks SM3 digests; SM3 is symmetric (Grover-margin, not Shor-broken) and is inventoried for completeness.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: hashcat test-module generator for mode 16500 (JWT cracking): signs JWTs with HMAC-SHA-256 (HS256, plus HS384/HS512) via hashlib to produce crackable vectors. HMAC-SHA-2 is Grover-weakened, not Shor-broken; the repo attacks these tokens rather than issuing them for protection.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: PBKDF2 is hashcat's most-used KDF: the OpenCL kernel library (inc_pbkdf2.h/cl), LUKS/TrueCrypt/VeraCrypt/PKCS#12 modules, vendored scrypt-jane (scrypt_pbkdf2) and yescrypt (PBKDF2_SHA256) reference code, and hundreds of test-vector generators. Iteration counts and PRFs come from the attacked formats (scrypt-jane's internal 1-iteration PRF chaining up to 16M+ in VeraCrypt). The KDFs are harvestable targets by design — that is the tool's purpose.

Grover-margin hashes; both attack target and internal component.

properties.name: pqs:context

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: SHA-3/Keccak across the tree: vendored scrypt-jane's Keccak implementation (keccak_round_constants, keccak_block in scrypt-jane-hash_keccak.h), the OpenCL SHA-3 kernel library, and the sha3 crate in the Rust dynamic_hash bridge (eval.rs recipe evaluation, inc_types.h constants). Strong Grover margin; attacked-format and bridge-provider inventory.

properties.name: pqs:context

Argon2id is the modern memory-hard KDF — Grover margin only; hashcat implements it to attack it.
